dedupe_keys.name: on the role of multi objective optimization to the transit network design problem

description: The implemented busOpt model combines multiobjective genetic search with single-objective weights inferred from human ratings of Pareto-front networks. It uses CARRIS/METRO fare records to infer demand and separately optimizes route topology and frequencies. The related thesis reports route reduction from 309 to 200, 59.8 percent less daily bus distance and unsatisfied demand changing from 0.7 to 1.3 percent, alongside lower travel/transfer objectives. These are simulated redesign outcomes. The project catalogue distinguishes busOpt from gtfs 2 osm, its road-network projection companion. Public repository metadata confirms busOpt code, while licence metadata differ between the catalogue’s unspecified GNU label and GitHub’s undetected licence. Coverage is limited to the source-described systems and experiments. The related Zenodo deposit provides descriptive metadata, with restricted document or data access and licence label not stated. Document rights do not establish software rights or access to the underlying observations. Only full descriptive metadata, file inventories and the project metadata catalogue were reviewed; no underlying measurements, code, paper or model archive was opened.
